title: post-upgrade hostNetwork daemonset reap causing iptables chain overwrite and tenant network isolation
creator: Lydia Chen
description: Summary: Several on-prem customers running hostNetwork-enabled nodeagents/daemonsets reported partial network isolation immediately after a Helm-based operator upgrade. Symptoms included pods unable to reach external services and cross-node pod-to-pod traffic drops. Investigation shows the operator's post-upgrade reconcile path re-applies a hostNetwork DaemonSet manifest which triggers kube-proxy/iptables chain reprogramming on affected nodes that use a CNI with custom iptables chains, overwriting provider-managed rules. This ticket tracks diagnosis, a surgical hotpatch to restore customer connectivity, and a durable fix plus rollout plan.
impact_details: Observed in 5 customers across 2 cloud regions and 3 on-prem clusters (private escalations). Outages lasted 7-45 minutes depending on manual remediation. Affected workloads: models with inter-pod streaming and runtimes using hostNetwork nodeagent. Root cause initially reproduced in lab cluster with Calico in masquerade=false mode when re-applying hostNetwork DS during a Helm post-upgrade hook.
repro_steps: 1) Install operator vX with hostNetwork nodeagent and Calico (masquerade=false) CNI. 2) Trigger Helm upgrade to vY which includes nodeagent image bump. 3) Observe post-upgrade reconcile re-apply of nodeagent DaemonSet; on nodes, iptables nat/RAW chains are replaced and kube-proxy rules are flushed. 4) Validate loss of cross-node pod connectivity and inability to reach external endpoints until iptables restored.
mitigation_plan:
Immediate mitigation (hotpatch):
- Provide a one-line remediation script for customers to restore prior iptables chains from saved snapshots or restart kube-proxy with preserved rules (documented in runbook).
- Push a temporary operator image that gates hostNetwork re-creates behind a preflight check and avoids replacing iptables chains (PR #1257).
- Notify impacted customers with status and ETA for hotfix.
Permanent fix:
- Change operator reconcile to perform strategic-merge patch on the DaemonSet instead of full reapply when hostNetwork=true.
- Add a preflight detector that validates CNI-managed iptables semantics and skips apply if mismatch.
- Add a post-upgrade network-validator job that runs lightweight connectivity probes and auto-triggers a rollback if checks fail.
acceptance_criteria:
- Lab reproduction no longer loses pod-to-pod connectivity after upgrade (Calico + masquerade=false).
- E2E test added to upgrade CI that runs hostNetwork DS apply path and verifies iptables invariants.
- Hotpatch image published and rolled to one non-production region with successful canary.
- Customer remediation script validated and included in private incident thread.
rollout_plan:
1) Merge hotpatch PR to release branch and cut operator-2025.08.1-hotfix image (canary).
2) Deploy to internal staging clusters and run network-validator probes.
3) Canary deploy to 2 low-risk customer clusters with close SRE support and telemetry watch.
4) Gradual rollout to remaining customers over 24-48h with rollback window and runbook on standby.
qa_steps:
- Run automated upgrade test with Calico/Flannel setups, hostNetwork enabled.
- Verify iptables chains persist and kube-proxy rules intact after reconcile.
- Run connectivity matrix (node->node, pod->external) for 30m post-upgrade.
notes: Design trade-offs discussed: full reapply is simpler but unsafe for hostNetwork/CNI combos. Strategic-merge reduces surface area but requires careful patch schema maintenance for future fields. Added preflight increases complexity but provides safer upgrades for regulated customers.
